chunks.title: South Campus - Delhi University
chunks.text:
South Campus
The University of Delhi started the south campus in 1973 as an effort to cope with its expansion. It moved to its present location on Benito Juarez Marg, near Dhaula Kuan, in 1984. Nearest Delhi Metro Station is Durgabai Deshmukh South Campus. The campus is spread across 28 hectares (69 acres). The various departments are located in the Faculty of Arts, Inter-disciplinary, Applied Sciences and the S.P. Jain Centre for Management Studies. South Campus has the following colleges: Aryabhatta College, Gargi College, Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, Jesus and Mary College, Maitreyi College, Motilal Nehru College, Ram Lal Anand College, Sri Venkateswara College, Rajdhani College, Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Institute of Home Economics, Pannalal Girdharlal Dayanand Anglo Vedic College, College of Vocational Studies.
When

chunks.title: South Campus - Delhi University
chunks.text:
ome Economics, Pannalal Girdharlal Dayanand Anglo Vedic College, College of Vocational Studies.
When the University of Delhi expanded in many directions to keep pace with a rapidly growing city, South Campus was established in 1973 to facilitate access for South Delhi residents. It moved to its present location on Benito Juarez Road, near Dhaula Kuan, in 1984. The Campus is now spread across 69 acres of green, hilly terrain and its buildings blend attractively with the natural surroundings. The various Departments are located in the Arts Faculty, the Faculty of Inter-disciplinary and Applied Sciences and the S.P. Jain Centre for Management Studies. Besides these, the Campus hosts a substantial library, a Health Centre, a bank, a post office, DTC Pass Section and administrative and examination blocks. South Campus also provides some

chunks.title: South Campus - Delhi University
chunks.text:
office, DTC Pass Section and administrative and examination blocks. South Campus also provides some residential quarters for faculty members and the non-teaching staff. Outstation students are offered accommodation in three hostels: the Geetanjali Hostel for Women, the Saramati Hostel for Men and the Aravalli P.G. Men’s Hostel.

Administration
The University of Delhi is a premier university of the country and is known for its high standards in teaching and research and attracts eminent scholars to its faculty. It was established in 1922 as a unitary, teaching and residential university by an act of the Central Legislative Assembly. The President of India is the Visitor, the Vice President is the Chancellor and the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India is the Pro-Chancellor of the University.
The Court, the Executive Council, the Academic Council and the Finance Committee are the authorities of the University. Following Officers of the University of Delhi are responsible for the administration of the University:

chunks.title: Vice Chancellor - Delhi University
chunks.text:
Vice Chancellor
Professor Yogesh Singh
Prof. Yogesh Singh, the 23rd Vice Chancellor of this century old University, assumed the charge of the Vice Chancellor on 8th October, 2021. He is an academician par excellence, a decisive leader with the courage to dream big and bring change, a beloved educationist who has touched the lives of innumerable number of students as well as his colleagues and peers.
‘Leadership is not about oneself; it's about investing in the growth of others.’ A quote that well expresses his passion and dedication towards the betterment of all. His leadership quality and administrative acumen and caliber has been exemplified by varied experience of leading academic institutions. He has a proven track record and experience of leading prestigious institutions of diverse nature – starting from a large size multi-faculty

chunks.title: Vice Chancellor - Delhi University
chunks.text:
nce of leading prestigious institutions of diverse nature – starting from a large size multi-faculty unitary university of forty thousand students in The Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, to technology oriented distinguished and reputed institutions like Netaji Subhas University of Technology (erstwhile Netaji Subhas Institute of Technology) and Delhi Technological University.
Prof. Singh became full Professor of Computer Engineering at the age of 35 in the University School of Information and Communication Technology, Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University, Delhi. He held many administrative responsibilities like Dean, University School of Engineering & Technology (2001-06), Dean, University School of Information and Communication Technology (2001-06), Chief Warden (2001-09), Proctor (2001-06), Director Student Welfare

chunks.title: Vice Chancellor - Delhi University
chunks.text:
munication Technology (2001-06), Chief Warden (2001-09), Proctor (2001-06), Director Student Welfare (2006-09), and Controller of Examinations (2006-11) of Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University, Delhi, before becoming the 16th Vice Chancellor of The Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, Gujarat, at the age of 45 years.
Prof. Yogesh Singh was the third Vice Chancellor of Delhi Technological University (July 14, 2016 to July 13, 2021) and was given a second term, which he continued up to Oct 7, 2021. He also served as the fifth Director of Netaji Subhas Institute of Technology, Delhi from December 31, 2014 to July 11, 2016. The Government of Delhi had given him the responsibility of these two premier institutions of the country the dual charge from Sept 23, 2015 to July 24, 2017. He was the sixteenth Vice Chancellor of The Maharaja

chunks.title: Vice Chancellor - Delhi University
chunks.text:
ual charge from Sept 23, 2015 to July 24, 2017. He was the sixteenth Vice Chancellor of The Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, Gujarat (July 07, 2011 to July 6, 2014) and the Government of Gujarat had given him the second term, which he continued up to December 29, 2014.
Prof. Singh received M.Tech. (Electronics & Communication Engineering) and Ph.D. (Computer Engineering) degrees from National Institute of Technology, Kurukshetra, Haryana. His receptivity, comprehensibility and logical thinking provided a rich learning experience as student, which in turn has made him a true representative of the student’s welfare, who understands and connects with them and believes in a transparent administration where the door is always open to everyone.
Prof. Singh has an impressive track record of quality teaching, innovation and research in

chunks.title: Vice Chancellor - Delhi University
chunks.text:
everyone.
Prof. Singh has an impressive track record of quality teaching, innovation and research in the area of Software Engineering, with ‘h’ index of 35, citation index of 4446 (reported by Google scholar as on June 27, 2024) and has supervised 23 Ph.Ds. He is listed as the third best amongst the most productive Indian authors for participating in Software Engineering Research reported in “Indian Computer Science Research Output during 1999-2008, Qualitative Analysis” Journal of Library & Information Technology, November 2010. He has more than 250 publications in International and National Journals/Conferences. His book, “Software Testing” published by Cambridge University Press, England (2011) is a well-received book nationally and internationally. He has also co-authored books on Software Engineering published by New Age

chunks.title: Vice Chancellor - Delhi University
chunks.text:
ally and internationally. He has also co-authored books on Software Engineering published by New Age International Delhi (2002), and Object Oriented Software Engineering published by PHI Learning, Delhi (2012). His exposure to various foreign universities, including those through YALE-INDIA LEADERSHIP PROGRAMME in Yale University, USA (2011), has provided him key insights into various facets of executive leadership and further honed his leadership skills.
Prof. Singh is Chairman of Governing Board of Information and Library Network (INFLIBNET) Centre, Gandhinagar, an Autonomous Inter-University Centre (IUC) of University Grants Commission, New Delhi (Ministry of Education, Government of India). He has been member of the Executive Committee of National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) with effect from October 03, 2019. He was

chunks.title: Vice Chancellor - Delhi University
chunks.text:
ee of National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) with effect from October 03, 2019. He was appointed as Independent Director of Gujarat State Petro Net Ltd. and Gujarat State Petroleum Corporations Ltd. (Government of Gujarat Undertakings) since May, 2013 and March, 2015 respectively. He is also serving as the Additional Director (Non-Executive, Independent Director) on the Board of Director of Gujarat Gas, a tenurial post of 5 years, with effect from 15 August, 2021.
Prof. Singh was Chairman, Central Regional Committee, All India Council for Technical Education, Bhopal (2011-14). He served as Member of the General Council of National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) (2012-15) and Member of the Governing Council of Association of Indian Universities (2016-17).
He has always had a holistic approach to education and an

chunks.title: Vice Chancellor - Delhi University
chunks.text:
ociation of Indian Universities (2016-17).
He has always had a holistic approach to education and an exemplary team player who has passed on his wisdom upon anyone who has crossed path with him with only one agenda, i.e. to impart knowledge. He is not just a visionary in his field but also a praiseworthy administrator. He has the courage to take decision where others hesitate, all for protecting the interest of the institution. He has done justice to all positions with such admirable grace and calmness that he is an inspiration to all.

He was nominated Asia Coordinator of the European Union 6th Framework Microdis Integrated Project, 2007 and was a delegate of the European Union to Poznan, Poland in United Nations Framework Climate Change Conference in 2008. He is recipient of the Indira Priyadarshini Vriksha Mitra National Award as Friends of Trees founder member, 1987 and the Inter-University Centre Associateship Award in Humanities and Social Sciences, 1996-1999, Certificate of Honour at the First France-India Meet on Psychiatry, Psychoanalysis and Psychotherapy, 2007, Plaque of Appreciation from Department of Sociology and Anthropology, Xavier University Ateneo de Cagayan de Oro City,

chunks.title: Vice Chancellor - Delhi University
chunks.text: tion from Department of Sociology and Anthropology, Xavier University Ateneo de Cagayan de Oro City, Philippines, 2008, and Certificate of Appreciation on his research on disaster impacts in Asia and Europe by Faculty of Public Health, University of Indonesia in 2009, among other honours and distinctions. He was the UGC Sap Advisory Committee member for the SV University, Tirupati, Vidhyasagar University, Midnapur, Central University of Hyderabad and Karnataka University Dharwad. He was the Task Force Member, Department of Biotechnology, Government of India. He has been in the panel of experts for Indian Council of Social Science Research and Member of Advisory Committee, Anthropological Survey of India, Ministry of Culture, Government of India. He has organized fifteen Conferences included one in the University of Hue, Vietnam in the

chunks.title: Vice Chancellor - Delhi University
chunks.text: of India. He has organized fifteen Conferences included one in the University of Hue, Vietnam in the year 2010. He is the current president of the Society for Indian Medical Anthropology, Mysore and specializes in the fields of Medical Anthropology, Himalayan Anthropology. Antibiotic Resistance and Qualitative Research Methods . His scientific publications are in the field of Medical Anthropology, Traditional Medicines, Shamanism, Impact of Disasters, Life Style Diseases and Antibiotic Resistance. Besides nine books, his papers numbering more than 150 have appeared in the journals such as World Development, The Eastern Anthropologists, Man in India, Journal of Biosocial Science, Journal of Southasian Disaster Studies, Journal of Anthropology, American Journal of Orthopsychiatry, European Academic Research, South Asian Anthropologist,

chunks.title: Vice Chancellor - Delhi University
chunks.text:
pology, American Journal of Orthopsychiatry, European Academic Research, South Asian Anthropologist, Prehospital and Disaster Medicine, International Journal of Human Science, Journal of Anthropological Survey of India, Indian Journal of Medical Research, Journal of Clinical Pharmacy and Therapeutics, Values in Health, Global Health Action, Family Practice, National Medical Journal of India and many more journals. He has supervised around 30 Ph.D. and around 25 M.Phil. students.

MSc Informatics
Masters of Science (Informatics) at the University of Delhi is the space where networking, telecommunication, and software collate to enable its students to cater to the growing demands of the industry and to merge as IICians with a brand mark of their own. The focus is on imparting relevant theoretical knowledge and practical skills in the global context. Students are admitted to the institute through a national-level entrance test followed by group discussions as well as personal interviews with a panel of experts.
The learning approach includes classroom lectures, tutorials, project assignments, seminars & presentations. With an exemplary history, IIC continues to provide achievers with an incessant desire for success.

Ph.D. at the Institute of Informatics and Communication focuses on providing interdisciplinary research opportunities in the field of your specialization inorder to solve research problems of domains intersecting with informatics. Ph.D. programs at IIC leverage holistic development of Research Scholars and encourage them to serve the society by contributing to the research areas they are passionate about.
IIC provides you with a high-grade and competitive research environment which lets you perform your research extensively. With state of art facilities like high-end computational equipment and access to e-libraries with reputed publications, it enables you to showcase your full potential. Scholars here work in collaboration with government agencies and industry professionals on various projects. Current researchers at IIC are

Holi Hooliganism Prevention-Committee
A committee has been formed to address Holi-related hooliganism in the department during the upcoming Holi festival. In the event of any untoward incident, the committee will handle the matter in accordance with the rules and regulations of the University of Delhi. The committee consists of the following members:
